caption:
🪖 The world's largest armies — 1933 → 1945.

In 1933 Germany's army was still held near the 100,000 men allowed by the Treaty of Versailles. Twelve years later, 51 million soldiers were under arms worldwide. Watch the order change: China leads first, at war long before Europe; Germany takes the top in 1939; and the war ends with the USSR and the United States at 12.5 and 12.1 million — the two powers that would split the world after it.

📊 Data: Correlates of War, National Material Capabilities v7.0. Occupied countries drop out while they had no army of their own; Chinese figures before 1937 are carried forward by the source.
